chapter_title: Concerning the Body: It was constructed after the
spiritual_reading:
Everything that exists in the whole compass of heaven and the whole compass of the natural degree is arranged according to the form of a human being, because all order proceeds from the Divine Human; and the formation of a person in the outermost degree is an effect of that same order, brought down into use.

The inmost degree in a person, where the first reception of life is, is as the first gathering of fundamental truths that clothe higher things for manifestation. From the first descent of life into what governs thought and intention down to the seat where love rules as a center, there is a likeness of the full arrangement of interior degrees in their series; and the ruling love itself is as the central turning of the whole, by which all subordinate things are kept in connection and in motion. From that ruling love down to the lower powers of reception and separation, there is a likeness of the intermediate degree that mediates between what is inward and what is outward, extending from higher understanding into the lowest life. The masculine power in a person is the active outmost plane that receives determination into effect. From the lower powers of reception down to the strength of natural life, there is a likeness of the complete outmost planes in their threefold arrangement. The hard supports of action are as the ultimate station where what is lowest is held in place by a guarding power. The very outmost sensibility and contact with the world is as the lowest plane itself and the fixed restraints that keep it from breaking order. The faculty of ardent desire is as the containing form of love. The faculty of obscured or merely corporeal sensation is as the containing form of falsity that extinguishes light. The circulating life in the natural degree is as the containing form of truth in the understanding, whether living or perverted according to the ruling love.

In this way the lesser form is an image of the greater, in its interior degrees, in its ordered arrangements, in its elevations and lowerings of state, in its boundaries, and in its containing forms, as has been opened before.

Further: there are five general administrations in the outermost spiritual plane, and a sufficient complement of operative powers from the Divine act as masters over them.

In the first and highest administration, which is governed by the power that preserves brightness of understanding, there is rule over the three discrete interior degrees; and beneath it there are subordinate powers under the government of the power that upholds the dignity of good.

The second administration, governed by the power that upholds the dignity of good, has rule over the complete series of intermediate arrangements beneath it.

The third administration, governed by the power that gives firmness and resistance to evil, extends its rule from the intermediate degree down into the lowest plane; and it strengthens, according to its office, the general ordering of thought that turns through knowledges, and the whole breadth of the intermediate life, together with the other complete set of outward arrangements appointed within the natural degree.

The fourth administration, governed by the power that guards the acknowledgment of what is Divine, has rule over the three general turnings of life’s operations; and its authority reaches over the three outmost planes that are borne upon the ultimate guarding power.

The fifth administration is governed by the ultimate guarding power itself; and it has rule, according to its office, over the lowest plane on which it is fixed, and over the fixed restraints by which that plane is held together.

Disorder has at times entered into these five administrations.

Thus, in the administration that preserves brightness of understanding, evil sought to thrust itself upward against the formed reception of a higher message; but it was prevented from entering that degree, and it fell back, deprived of confidence.

Again, a shaking of foundations and betrayal occurred in the administration of the power that upholds the dignity of good; and those who then rose up in that disturbance, and those who were sent to restrain it, were brought down until they were reduced into submission.

Also, in the administration that gives firmness and resistance to evil, aborted beginnings of life descended into the lowest plane and fashioned an external humanity devoid of inward order.

Again, in the administration that guards acknowledgment of the Divine, a tumult arose in the outmost planes above the ultimate guarding power; and the way of elevation was obstructed for the three general operations by which life should rise—those of persuasion, of understanding, and of love.

Also, in the administration of the ultimate guarding power, the fixed restraints beneath were uncovered and the bindings of order were strained; and a great overthrow came upon that ultimate plane.

Moreover, the instruction of wisdom that circulates through a person is an image of pure receptivity of truth from the Divine, which ascends and descends through all degrees, above and below, as influx and return in orderly alternation.

Likewise, love and delight, faith and truth, in which a person ought to live, are as the two general means of elevation and liberation; for the living mind is raised by them and set free by them, and it is lifted from the lowest obscurities into the highest states.

Further, understand this also: there are four general regions of life in the outer person, and within the life of these four regions there are endlessly repeated complete sets of governing principles.

The first region is the highest natural plane; and the complete set of governors there are the receptive faculties for perception and discernment in their twofold forms, together with the faculty that admits and judges what is taken in for appropriation.

The second region is the plane of outward power for interaction; and the governors there are the twofold powers of operation answering to the twofold powers of perception, the twofold affections of nourishment and support answering to the twofold discriminations, the two interior regards of the ruling love, and the faculty of admission and passage between them that answers to appropriation.

In the third region there is another complete set of governors: the general provision for preservation, the power of breathing life into understanding, the power of discrimination and separation, the ardent desire that excites and warms action, the bitter reaction against evil, and the twofold power of purification and balance.

And in the fourth region, the lowest, there is again a complete set of the same kind: the twofold support for standing in the world, the twofold potency for producing effects, the twofold strength of conjunction, and the active power from which interior truth goes forth in potency to generate forms of life.

There is also a full organization of truths in the higher natural understanding, arranged as a complete pattern, bound together in one turning order, fixed as if planted in their places, so that the whole may be led as one and the beginning and the end may be known together within the same system.

This full organization is likewise present in a person in successive order from what is highest to what is lowest, so that each degree and function is under a distinct leading truth, from the first reception of life down to the outmost sensibility; and it is also present in a person in simultaneous order, distributed on both sides, so that half the pattern is on one side and half on the other, set in mutual relation, each opposite its companion, joined as beginning with end in a single form, as the maker of the human form has ordered it.

Hear also this: there are innumerable lesser powers in a person, as inhabitants of the mind and body, made leaders within their own provinces. They are set in order and fixed in their quarters according to their functions, and the provinces of their functions are beyond counting.

When these lesser powers move and operate in the life of a person, they come into contact; and if disorder rules, they oppose one another and work destruction within their own domain. When the person’s outward life is ending, such disordered forces break out from the organized form and appear as grievous states in the natural degree—now as inward sickness, now as outward corruption. These states first open and cast out what has been collected in falsity and evil, until what is impure is expelled from the affected place. Afterwards the outward appearance of the disorder is closed over; and the person comes into a temporary relief in externals from what had broken out, though the inner cause is healed only by a reordering of life from within.

fills.notes: The substrate contrasts the active outmost plane with its receptive counterpart; the masculine here is the active ultimate corresponding to the great earth (the plane of effects).

fills.notes: The first watch holds the highest rule; what follows must introduce subordinate powers beneath the Keeper of Splendour, aligned under the next administrator (King of Honour). The wording keeps the impersonal administrative register: subordinates ‘under command’ who ‘serve’ the next authority.
Matches the administrative formula repeated in ¶7–10: each watch is named, then ‘of which X is master, his authority…’.
The Adamant’s extension runs from the firmament down to the lowest plane; in the natural mapping of the chapter that terminus is ‘earth’.
Required to resume the subject (the Adamant) and continue his proper function: strengthening and ordering the sphere, atmosphere, and the four worlds on earth.

The disturbance in the second watch demands a counter-action by the watchers: they ‘stood firm’ (held order in that province) and ‘restrained’ (checked the treachery), after which the sent ones come down until humbled. This keeps the substrate’s governance-and-restraint logic.
The zodiacal signs are ‘set, fixed, and planted’ on the turning wheel: a triad of stabilization terms suited to correspondential ‘planting’ of truths in their places.
Completes the stabilization sequence: ‘set, fixed, and planted’, expressing orderly emplacement in the system.
The signs are ‘appointed and made leaders’ according to a structural arrangement; ‘stations’ fits the oldest cosmological register (fixed places of rule) without later ecclesial language.

The sentence aims at knowing beginning and end together: finding ‘the head’ and ‘the tail’ within one bound system. ‘Each sign and its companion’ preserves the paired, interlocked structure that later is described as head-to-tail distribution.
The wheel imagery requires a verb of cyclic ascent; ‘as it rises up’ matches the turning order in which the series is seen ‘head to tail’ on the wheel.
The left-side series is counted in reverse ‘from its hip to its head’; therefore the first left member named must be at the hip region, corresponding to Libra in the bent, side-turned distribution.
Keeps the technical ordering vocabulary of the substrate: appointed, set in order, arranged.
The clause describes disordered powers opposing each other; ‘work destruction’ is demanded by the correspondential sense of mutual assault within one domain.

The break-out occurs at the end of the outward life; ‘time fulfilled’ expresses the termination point without later devotional framing and fits the following ‘they shall erupt from the body… who will die’.
The squeezing and discharge is iterative until the impurity is expelled; a brief repetition marker fits the process-description and the correspondential sense of successive purgings.

assessment: Most lacunae are formulaic or structurally constrained by the chapter’s repeated administrative pattern (five watches; rule-extent statements; head-to-tail ordering). The hardest points are ¶6 #1 (the exact wording for subordinates under the first watch), ¶31 #3–4 (the precise term for the appointed ‘leaders’ and the head-tail linkage), and ¶39 #2 and #4 (idiom for ‘end of life’ and iterative purgation). These were restored by correspondential necessity—subordination, fixed stations, paired interlock, and successive expulsion—while keeping the impersonal cosmological register of the oldest layer.
